author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Silent Shadow
challenge.description: #reliability_ruth# insists on a fully automated and governed shadow deployment to validate model behavior before release, while #automation_alex# argues that the shadow environment is redundant and should be removed entirely to reduce infrastructure complexity. #automation_alex# has a red line against maintaining any shadow infrastructure and will not move on this point.

output.content: We need the canary and A/B testing pipelines to run automatically so we catch performance regressions the moment they appear. The current manual checks are too slow for our release cadence. I want the system to validate model behavior in a shadow environment before any traffic shifts. The more automated these validation steps are, the better, because I need to see real world impact without waiting for a scheduled review. I am asking for full automation of these checks to ensure we can iterate quickly on reliability issues. The goal is to have a continuous feedback loop that flags any degradation instantly, allowing us to fix problems before they affect end users. This level of automation is essential for maintaining the service quality our clients expect.
output.reclassify_reason: The text explicitly states that the author wants the validation steps to be as automated as possible ('the more automated... the better') to achieve a continuous feedback loop, indicating that exceeding the baseline request for automation would make them happier.
